findings: Game Mode: the session card always said "The previous display lease is stale", although the reports show the reservation of DP-1 at Game Mode start. Bazzite's gamescope (terra-gamescope) carries %caps(cap_sys_nice=eip); such a process is not dumpable and /proc/PID/exe is refused (EACCES) even to its own user, which the check needed.

Host: launch 3 was ready after 61.88 s ("Host runtime interrupted" was logged during the start); 3.06 s later "A different SteamVR process appeared" ended the session, and six Stops over the next 80 s failed with "SteamVR ownership changed" until SteamVR was closed on the host.

Eye tracking: about 17 gaze samples a second (the camera helper paced the stream at one picture per 50 ms, only the first after each pause); Baballonia's One Euro filter at its defaults (0.5 Hz, speed 3).

Stream: 3200 x 3200 per eye; SteamVR showed it at reduced rate (37.5 fps) for the whole session, the integrated GPU at about 940 of 2700 MHz and about 20 W (a power limit); SteamVR's background reprojection was off on the headset PC.
Host: HTTP Error 403 logged at every retry once the client stopped sharing its report (it does so only during a session and a minute after).
Controllers: tracking dropouts reported by SteamVR on the headset PC (tracking_result 101), not from VROSTBridge.
changes: launcher/game_mode.py gamescope_alive: the reserving gamescope identified by /proc/PID/stat (start time), status (real and effective UID), cmdline (gamescope with the leased --lease-connector) and, where readable, the program link
